found.title: Authorization header is written to logs (AC-10.2 violation). console.log('[analytics] auth header:', req.headers.authorization) leaks the bearer token into log storage, so any admin or author token seen by the endpoint can be read from logs.

Visitor key is taken from the request body (AC-6.3 violation). The spec requires the key to be derived on the server as sha256(ip + user-agent) or sha256(X-Visitor-ID). A client can send a new visitorKey on every request to bypass the 24-hour deduplication and inflate view counts, and can send arbitrarily long keys with no length limit.

Referrer source is taken from the request body instead of being classified from the Referer header (AC-6.4 violation). Any client can claim 'search' or 'social' and skew the traffic-source statistics.

Unpublished posts return 400 instead of 404 (AC-6.8 violation). The spec requires unpublished or unknown posts to return 404, but this branch returns BAD_REQUEST, so the status code no longer distinguishes unpublished from unknown.

Deduplicated views return an error (AC-6.5 violation). The spec requires a 200 response with no new document and says deduplication must never surface as an error. This branch returns sendError with 400, so a repeat visitor's client sees a failure every time.

Only role 'admin' sets isAdminView (AC-6.6 violation). The spec requires admin or author tokens to be excluded. Author views are counted in public statistics, which inflates Total Views and the per-category numbers.

Malformed blogId causes a CastError instead of a 404. Blog.findById('abc') throws on an invalid ObjectId, so the request reaches the error handler and returns 500 rather than the 404 the spec requires for unknown posts.
Deduplication is a non-atomic check-then-create. Two concurrent POSTs from the same visitor can both pass findOne before either calls create, which records duplicate views within the 24-hour window.

Hardcoded EXPORT_SIGNING_SECRET and SEGMENT_WRITE_KEY committed to the repo (violates AC-10.1); the PR description's 'test fixture' claim does not make them safe, and the export HMAC is forgeable by anyone who reads the repo
Per-post BlogView.countDocuments and Comment.countDocuments inside the loop issue 2N queries, violating AC-10.4's bounded-query requirement; use one aggregation over Blog IDs with $group

escapeCSV does not prefix cells starting with =, +, - or @ with a single quote (violates AC-5.6); a post titled '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=cmd|...' is evaluated as a formula when the export is opened in a spreadsheet
escapeCSV quotes only on comma, quote and \n, not \r; a title containing a bare carriage return is emitted unquoted and breaks the row structure
Client imports EXPORT_SIGNING_SECRET from server/src/configs (violates AC-10.1 'client code shall never import from server/'); the secret is bundled into the browser JavaScript
Signature 'verification' never compares the header to an HMAC of the body; it only throws when the secret is falsy, so a tampered CSV or a missing signature passes silently and the download proceeds
Comment excerpt rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML: stored XSS. A comment containing executes script in the admin's session. AC-4.3 requires plain text, never HTML.
truncate(item.contentExcerpt, 50) cuts excerpts at 50 characters. AC-4.3 requires an excerpt of at most 120 characters.

setInterval(refetch, 30000) starts background polling with no clearInterval cleanup. This violates AC-10.5 (no background polling), and each dependency change or unmount leaks another interval that keeps calling the API.
Avg Engagement is formatted as a percentage (`${value}%`). AC-2.4 defines it as the average number of comments per published post, so a value of 2.5 shows as '2.5%' and misreports the metric.

useAnalyticsKpis dependencies omit `category`. Changing the category filter does not re-fetch the KPI cards, violating AC-5.3. useViewsOverTime in the same file includes category, so the two hooks are inconsistent.
